inputs.text:
The US-Israel-Iran conflict is a warning that a nation which relies on imported crude leaves its working families exposed to turmoil beyond its control. When fuel prices rise, ordinary households pay first. Cutting excise duties is a sensible way to relieve that pressure, but governments still have a duty to manage revenue responsibly—not quietly push the cost onto families later.

Energy security should come before fashionable promises that leave the country dependent and vulnerable. A responsible nation protects its households by building a dependable energy system and putting the interests of its people first.

output.main_topic: Energy dependence, household exposure to fuel-price turmoil, and energy security
